question.text:
In the given text, the blanks are numbered $\text{(i)-(iv)}$. Select the best match for all the blanks.

Prof. $\text{P}$  __(i)__   merely a man who narrated funny stories. __(ii)__ in his blackest moments he was capable of self-deprecating humor.

Prof. $\text{Q}$ ___(iii)__ a man who hardly narrated funny stories. ___(iv)___ in his blackest moments was he able to find humor.

  1. (i) was (ii) Only (iii) wasn't (iv) Even
  2. (i) wasn't (ii) Even (iii) was (iv) Only
  3. (i) was (ii) Even (iii) wasn't (iv) Only
  4. (i) wasn't (ii) Only (iii) was (iv) Even

The expression $\dfrac{(x+y) - |x-y|}{2}$ is equal to :

  1. The maximum of $x$ and $y$
  2. The minimum of $x$ and $y$
  3. $1$
  4. None of the above

Two alloys $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ contain copper and zinc in the ratio $7: 2$ and $5: 3$ respectively. How many kg of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ must be melted in order to get an alloy of $44 \mathrm{~kg}$ containing copper and Zinc in the ratio $3: 1?$

  1. $24 \mathrm{~kg}, 20 \mathrm{~kg}$
  2. $30 \mathrm{~kg}, 14 \mathrm{~kg}$
  3. $28 \mathrm{~kg}, 16 \mathrm{~kg}$
  4. $36 \mathrm{~kg}, 8 \mathrm{~kg}$

For all non-negative integers $x$ and $y, f(x, y)$ is defined as below

  • $f(0, y) = y + 1$
  • $f(x + 1, 0) = f(x, 1)$
  • $f(x + 1,y + 1) = f(x, f(x + 1, y))$

Then, what is the value of $f(1, 2)?$

  1. Two
  2. Four
  3. Three
  4. Cannot be determined

Refer to the following pie chart and answer the questions that follow.


The amount spent on $\text{LABOUR}$ exceeds the amount spent on $\text{STEEL}$ by?

  1. $5 \%$ of total cost
  2. $10 \%$ of total cost
  3. $12 \%$ of total cost
  4. $15\%$ of total cost

​​If ' $\rightarrow$ ' denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [smile $\rightarrow$ giggle $\rightarrow$ laugh] is analogous to [disapprove $\rightarrow$ _________$\rightarrow$ chide]

Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?

  1. reprove
  2. praise
  3. reprise
  4. grieve

There are $150$ students in a class. The number of students who play Cricket, Hockey, and Basketball are $125, 130, 135$ respectively. If $5$ students do not play any of the three games, the number of students playing all the three games must be at least

  1. $90$
  2. $95$
  3. $100$
  4. $105$

Let $x, y$ be two positive numbers such that $x + y =1.$ Then, the minimum value of $\left(x+ \dfrac{1}{x} \right)^2 + \left(y + \dfrac{1}{y}\right)^2$ is

  1. $12$
  2. $20$
  3. $12.5$
  4. $13.3$

A circular sheet of paper is folded along the lines in the directions shown. The paper, after being punched in the final folded state as shown and unfolded in the reverse order of folding, will look like _______.

$\text{A}$ can complete a piece of work in $4$ days. $\text{B}$ takes double the time taken by $\text{A, C}$ takes double that of $\text{B},$ and $\text{D}$ takes double that of $\text{C}$ to complete the same task. They are paired in groups of two each. One pair takes two-thirds the time needed by the second pair to complete the work. Which is the first pair?

  1. $\text{A, B}$
  2. $\text{A, C}$
  3. $\text{B, C}$
  4. $\text{A, D}$

The diagram shows two TCP senders at left and the corresponding receivers at right. Both senders use TCP Tahoe. Assume that the MSS is $1 \mathrm{~KB}$, that the one-way propagation delay for both connections is $100 \mathrm{~ms}$ and that the link joining the two routers has a bandwidth of $16\; \mathrm{Mb} / \mathrm{s}$. Let $c w n d_1$ and $c w n d_2$ be the values of the senders' congestion windows.

Please note that TCP Tahoe goes to slowstart on triple duplicate ACK or timeout. It sets threshold to $\frac{c w n d}{2}$ and cwnd to $1$

Assume that the link buffer overflows whenever $cwnd_1+cwnd_2 \geq 600 \mathrm{~KB}$. Buffer overflow is a situation of packet loss.

Let Initially both $S_!$ and $S_2$ are in slow start with $cwnd_1=250 \mathrm{~KB}$ and $cwnd_2=50 \mathrm{~KB}$.
After $20$ RTTs, approximately what are the values of $c w n d_1$ and $c w n d_2$?

 

 

  1. $cwnd_1$ is about $260 \mathrm{~KB}\;cwnd_2$ is about $62 \mathrm{~KB}$
  2. $cwnd_1$ is about $266 \mathrm{~KB}\; cwnd_2$ is about $64 \mathrm{~KB}$
  3. $cwnd_1$ is about $262 \mathrm{~KB}\; cwnd_2$ is about $64 \mathrm{~KB}$
  4. $cwnd_1$ is about $266 \mathrm{~KB}\; cwnd_2$ is about $66 \mathrm{~KB}$

Consider the following declaration of C code where  $\text{a}$ and $\text{p}$ are variables inside $\text{main}$ function.

int a[10];
int (*p)[10];
p = &a;

If variable $\textsf{a}$ is not initialized with integers  then which of the following may give a run-time error?

  1. (p+1)
  2. (p+1)[2]
  3. p[2]
  4. *p[2]

Consider the following undirected graph G. Which of the statements below is/are true?

  1. $G$ has a clique of size 4
  2. $G$ has the chromatic number 2
  3. G has a Hamiltonian circuit
  4. G has an Eulerian circuit

Consider the following function $\textsf{printNthNode()}.$

void printNthNode(Node *head){
    Node *p, *q;
    p = q= head;
    while(q){
        p = p->next;
        q = q->next ? q->next->next : NULL;
    }
    printf("%d", p->data);
}

We pass the head of the singly linked list to the above function. Which of the option(s) is/are correct about a linked list of length $n\; (n\geq 2)?$

The length of a linked list is the number of nodes in it.

  1. Function prints $n/2$ node value if $n$ is even
  2. Function prints $n/2 +1$ node value if $n$ is even
  3. Function prints $(n-1)/2 +1$ node value if $n$ is odd
  4. Function prints $(n+1)/2 +1$ node value if $n$ is odd

Consider a direct mapped cache having $\log _2 \mathrm{P}$ bits as tag and block size of $\mathrm{M}$ bytes. Suppose the main memory comprises $\mathrm{C}$ blocks. What should the cache size be $? ($Assume that $\text{P, M,}$ and $\text{C}$ are powers of $2.)$

  1. $\text{C / P}$
  2. $\text{M C / P}$
  3. $\text{M P}$
  4. $\mathrm{M} \log _2 \mathrm{P}$

Consider the following code:

I0: r1 = r2 + r3;
I1: r3 = r1 + r1;
I2: r4 = r1 + r3
I3: r1 = r2 * r3;
I4: r3 = r1 / r4;

Identify all data dependencies (potential data hazards) in the given code snippet.

  1. Number of RAW dependencies $=6$
  2. Number of WAR dependencies $=6$
  3. Number of WAW dependencies $=2$
  4. Number of RAR dependencies $=7$

Suppose that stacks and queues are provided as opaque data types, offering only operations to add elements, to remove elements, and to test for emptiness. Suppose that a programmer wants to count the number of elements in a given stack or queue $\text{C}$, which is currently in some state $t$, using only one auxiliary stack or queue $\text{D}$.

The structures $\text{C}$ and $\text{D}$ can be used in any way possible based on the methods they offer, but $\text{C}$ must be restored to its state $t$ after counting its elements.

Counting elements as described above is possible for which of the following data types?

  1. $\text{C}$ is a queue and $\mathrm{D}$ is a queue.
  2. $\text{C}$ is a stack and $\mathrm{D}$ is a stack.
  3. $\text{C}$ is a queue and $\mathrm{D}$ is a stack.

 

  1. None
  2. I and II only
  3. I and III only
  4. I, II and III only

Assume a four-CPU machine. Assume that the system provides a user-level threading package and no kernel-level threading. How many CPUs can a single process use, if the process has four user-level threads?

ABC

  1. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$
  2. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}$
  3. $\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}$
  4. $\mathrm{AB}\rightarrow \mathrm{C}$

If we have $m$ vectors $u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_m$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, then we can form the matrix $\text{A}$ whose columns are $u_1, \ldots, u_m$. Let $\text{B}$ be the echelon form of $\text{A}$.

Suppose we are given the following matrix $\text{B}$ :
$$
\left(\begin{array}{cccc}
3 & 0 & -1 & 5 \\
0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0
\end{array}\right)
$$
Since $\text{B}$ is the echelon form of $\text{A}$, both $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ have the same size $-3$ rows and $4$ columns.


Which if the following is/are CORRECT?

  1. $\left\{u_1, u_3\right\}$ are linearly independent.
  2. There exist a vector $w \in \mathbb{R}^n$ that we can add to the set $\left\{u_1, \ldots, u_m\right\}$ to guarantee that $\text{A} x=b$ has a solution for any $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$.
  3. $\text{A} x=0$ and $\text{B} x=0$ have the same solutions.
  4. If we erase the last row of zeros in $\text{B}$ then the columns of the resulting matrix would be linearly independent.

Which of the following statements is/are true?
I. Shifting a twos-complement integer right by one bit, and filling from the left with 0 , is always equivalent to dividing by 2.
II. An integer's ones-complement representation is never identical to its twos-complement representation.

  1. I only
  2. II only
  3. I and II Both
  4. None of the above

The set of Finite languages is closed under?

  1. Union
  2. Intersection
  3. Complement
  4. Reverse

What will be the output of the following C program?

#include<stdio.h>
int main()
{
    static int p[] = {1, 2, 3, 0, 5, 6};
    static int *q[] = {p+2, p+1, p, p+3, p+4, p+5};
    static int **r[] = {q+4, q+5, q+1, q, q+2, q+3};
    int ***pt;
    pt = r + 2;
    printf("%d", ***(pt+3)-**(q+1));
}

Suppose we have a relation $R(A, B)$ with one tuple, both of whose components are NULL:

  1. (NULL,NULL)
  2. (NULL,0)
  3. $(\mathrm{NULL}, 1)$
  4. Empty Table

Which of the following strings match the regular expression $a^\ast b b(a b \mid b a)^\ast$

  1. $a b b$
  2. $aaba$
  3. $abba$
  4. $bbbaab$

A bit counting machine reads a binary input vector $(a, b, c, d)$ and produces a binary number $(\text{S}_{2},\text{S}_{1},\text{S}_{0})$ that counts the number of $1’\text{s}$ in the input bits. For example when $(a, b, c, d)=(0,1,1,1)$, we have output $(\text{S}_{2},\text{S}_{1},\text{S}_{0})=(0,1,1)$, and when $(a, b, c, d)=(1,0,1,0)$, we have output $(\text{S}_{2},\text{S}_{1},\text{S}_{0})=(0,1,0)$.

Let $\mathrm{Y(a,b,c,d)}$ be a boolean function such that $Y$ is $1$ for any input combination $(a,b,c,d)$ if and only if both $S_1,S_0$ are both $1$ for that input combination.

The number of Prime Implicants in $\text{Y}?$

Let $\mathrm{L}$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$. The equivalence relation $\sim_{\mathrm{L}}$ on the set $\Sigma^\ast $ of all finite length strings over $\Sigma$ is defined by $u_{\sim L} v$ if and only if for all $w \in \Sigma^\ast $ it is the case that $u w \in \text{L}$ if and only if $v w \in \text{L}$. Suppose that $\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{M})$ is the language accepted by a deterministic finite automaton $\text{M}$. For each $u \in \Sigma^\ast $, let $s(u)$ be the unique state of $\text{M}$ reached from the initial state after inputting the string $u.$
Now consider the following statements :

  1. $s(u)=s(v)$ implies $u \sim_\text{L} v$.
  2. $u \sim_{\mathrm{L}} v$ implies $s(u)=s(v)$.

Which of the above statements is correct?

  1. Only $1$
  2. Only $2$
  3. Both
  4. None

Consider the open statement
$$
p(x, y): \quad y-x=y+x^{2}
$$
where the universe for each of the variables $x, y$ comprises all integers. Determine the truth value for each of the following statements.
Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. $\exists y $ $(p(1, y))$
  2. $\forall x \exists y$ $ p(x, y)$
  3. $\exists y \forall x$ $ p(x, y)$
  4. $\forall y \exists x$ $ p(x, y)$
What is the sum of the local miss rate for $\text{L2}\$, \text{L1}\$,$ and the global miss rate of $\text{L2}\$?($Round off each to $2$ decimal places $)$ ________.

Given any non-empty finite set $A$, let $\mathcal{P}(A)$ be the power set of $A$ and $\mathcal{C}$ any partition of $A$. Which of the following statements are always true?

  1. $\exists S \in \mathcal{C}$ such that $S \subseteq \mathcal{P}(A)$.
  2. $\exists S \in \mathcal{P}(A)$ such that $S \in \mathcal{C}$.
  3. $\exists S \in A$ such that $\{S\} \in \mathcal{C}$.

 

  1. Only (i).
  2. Only (ii).
  3. Only (i) and (ii).
  4. Only (i) and (iii).

We have an AVL tree that contains the integers $1,2,3, \ldots 20$. We do not know what order the values were inserted into the tree. Possible values that could appear as the root.

  1. $3$
  2. $5$
  3. $7$
  4. $16$

Which of the following statements about datagrams sent by a node in a network using $\textsf{IPv4}$ protocol is (are) true?

  1. Datagrams at the source must be the size of the smallest maximum transmission unit (MTU) of all the links on a path to the destination.
  2. Datagrams may be fragmented during routing.
  3. Datagrams are reassembled only at the destination.

 

  1. I only
  2. II only
  3. III only
  4. II and III

If $g(n)= \Omega(n)$ and $h(n)=O(n)$ then $g(n) . h(n)$ will be -

  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $O(n)$
  3. $\Omega(n)$
  4. None of these

What is the time complexity of the code given?

int i = 1, j = 2;
while (i <= n) {
    sum += 1;
    i = i * j;
    j = j * 2;
}
  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$
  3. $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$
  4. $\Theta\left((\log n)^{2}\right)$

Suppose that two relations $R(A, B)$ and $S(A, B)$ have exactly the same schema. Consider the following equalities in relational algebra?

  1. $\quad R \cap S=R-(R-S)$
  2. $R \cap S=S-(S-R)$
  3. $R \cap S=R$ NATURAL-JOIN $S$
  4. $\mathrm{R} \cap \mathrm{S}=\mathrm{R} \times \mathrm{S}$


Which of the equalities hold in relational algebra?

 

  1. I only
  2. I and II only
  3. I, II and III
  4. I, II, III and IV

If a term in the expansion of $\left(2 x^{2}+\frac{m}{y}\right)^{3}$ is $\frac{54 x^{2}}{y^{2}}$, the value of $m$ is

  1. 2
  2. 3
  3. 4
  4. 5

Let $\text{C}=A^{\top} \text{A}-\text{A A}^{\top}$. Where $\text{A}$ is matrix of size $n \times n.$

Which of the following is true?

  1. $\text{C}$ is a symmetric matrix only if $\text{A}$ is symmetric matrix
  2. $\text{C}$ is a skew-symmetric matrix only if $\text{A}$ is skew-symmetric matrix
  3. $\text{C}$ is a symmetric matrix
  4. $\text{C}$ is a skew-symmetric matrix

The procedure operates on three arrays $\text{A} [0 \dots 99], \text{B}[0 \dots 99]$ and $\text{C} [0 \dots 99],$ which are initialized with integer values.

procedure mystery () {
    for (i=0; i<100; i++) {C[i] = A[i];}
    p=99;
    for (i=0; i<100; i++) {
        B[p] = C[0];
        p = p-1;
        for (j=1; j<100; j++){
            C[j - 1] = C[j];
        }
    }
}

When the procedure terminates, which of the following statements can be asserted about the array $\text{B}?$

  1. All elements of $\text{B}$ are equal to $\text{A}[0]$

  2. $\text{B}$ contains the elements of $\text{A}$ sorted in descending order

  3. All values of $\text{B}$ are the same

  4. $\text{B}$ contains the elements of $\text{A}$ in reverse order

Consider a system which uses a hard disk for storage. The task of managing the hard disk comes under the operating system. It is very important to keep track of occupancy of the hard disk i.e., which block is empty or which block is already occupied. A particular disk unit uses a bit string to record the vacancy and occupancy of its tracks, with $0$ denoting vacant and $1$ denoting occupied. A $32$ bit segment of this string has hexadecimal value $\textsf{F1E0FA36}.$ The percentage of empty track for the corresponding part of the disk, to the nearest percentage is ___________ ( upto two decimal places).

Which of the following statements are true?

  1. Let $G$ be a simple, undirected graph with 6 vertices, 5 edges and no cycles. Then it is not possible to have only one vertex in $G$ with degree 1.
  2.  Let $G$ be a simple, undirected graph with $n$ vertices and $e$ edges. If $G$ is not connected, then $e<(n-1)$.
  3.  All cycles in the graph $K_{3,4}$ have an even number of edges.

 

  1. Only (i).
  2. Only (i) and (ii).
  3. Only (i) and (iii).
  4. All of (i), (ii) and (iii).

Consider the JK Flip flop made using NAND gates given below

What is the characteristic equation of JK Flip flop? $(\text{Q}$ represents the present state and $\text{Q}_n$ represents the next state of the flip flop)

  1. $\text{Q}_n=\overline{\text{J}} \text{Q + KQ}$
  2. $\text{Q}_n= \text{J} \overline{\text{Q}}+\overline{\text{K}} \text{Q}$
  3. $\text{Q}_n= \text{JQ} +\overline{\text{K}} \text{Q}$
  4. $\text{Q}_n=\overline{\text{J}} \text{Q + K} \overline{\text{Q}}$

The following plot shows a function $y$ which varies linearly with $x$. The value of the integral $I= \displaystyle{}\int_1^2 y d x$ is

  1. $1.0$
  2. $2.5$
  3. $4.0$
  4. $5.0$

Which Boolean expression is equivalent to the following circuit diagram?
 

  1. $X=A^{\prime}+(A \oplus B)$
  2. $X=A+(A \oplus B)^{\prime} \quad$
  3. $X=A \oplus(A+B)^{\prime}$
  4. $X=A+\left(A \oplus B^{\prime}\right)$

The page table is moved to the main memory and accessed via a TLB. Each main memory access takes $50$ ns and each TLB access takes $10$ ns. Each virtual memory access involves:

  • mapping VPN to PPN using TLB $(10$ ns)
  • if TLB miss: mapping VPN to PPN using page map in main memory $(50$ ns)
  • accessing main memory at appropriate physical address $(50$ ns)

Assuming no page faults (i.e. all virtual memory is resident) what TLB hit rate is required for an average virtual memory access time of $61 \mathrm{~ns}$.

  1. $0.98$
  2. $0.95$
  3. $0.96$
  4. $0.90$

Write the following binary number as an $\textsf{IEEE}$ single-precision float: $0.10101010 \ldots,$ that is, bits $10$ repeating infinitely many times to the right of the binary point.

  1. $\textsf{0xAAAAAAAA}$
  2. $\textsf{0x3F2AAAAA}$
  3. $\textsf{0x3FFAAAAA}$
  4. $\textsf{0x332FAAAA}$

Using the grammar and the associated semantic actions, calculate the value of $\mathrm{G} . \mathrm{p}$ after parsing the expression $\neg(A \wedge(A \Rightarrow B))$.

$\mathrm{G \rightarrow F}$$\mathrm{G.p = F.p}$
$\mathrm{F\rightarrow F_1 \wedge F_2}$$\mathrm{F.p = And(F_1.p, F_2.p)}$
$\mathrm{F\rightarrow F_1 \vee F_2}$$\mathrm{F.p = Or(F_1.p, F_2.p)}$

$\mathrm{F\rightarrow F_1 \implies F_2}$$\mathrm{F.p = Or(Not(F_1.p), F_2.p)}$

  1. $\operatorname{And}(A,\operatorname{Or}(A, B))$
  2. $\operatorname{Not}(\operatorname{And}(A, \operatorname{Or}(\operatorname{Not}(A), B)))$
  3. $\operatorname{Or}(A, \operatorname{Not}(\operatorname{And}(A, B)))$
  4. $\operatorname{Not}(\operatorname{Or}(A, \operatorname{And}(\operatorname{Not}(A), B)))$

What will be the output of the following lines of code?

int i = 0;
int j = 0;
char *s = "ceded";
while (s[i] != '\0') {
    j = j + s[i] - 'b';
    i = i + 1;
}
printf("%d %d\n", i, j);
  1. $5\; 11$
  2. $4\; 16$
  3. $5\; 16$
  4. $4 \;11$

A student can register for at most $p$ courses and each course can have at most $v$ students. Each student is enrolled to at least one course and each course has at least one student.

This schema is normalized into three tables:
$\textbf{Student, Registers, Courses}$

The number of tuples in student and course tables are $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Which of the following need not be correct?

  1. $Y \geq 1$
  2. $Y \leq p ^* X$
  3. $X \geq v ^*  Y$
  4. $X > 0$

Due to the current $\text{COVID}$ pandemic conditions, assume that positive or negative status of any individual are equally likely. There are $3$ members in a family. If one of the members has tested $\text{COVID}$ positive, the conditional probability that at least $2$ members are $\text{COVID}$ positive is _______ (rounded off to three decimal places).

Given a binary search tree $\mathrm{T}$, we insert $n$ elements, but when the size of tree become doubled then we balance the tree. for example if we insert $2^{k-1}$ element then when the size become to $2^{k}$ then we balance $\mathrm{T}.$ what is tightest time complexity insert $n$ items in such tree?

  1. $\mathrm{O}(n)$
  2. $\mathrm{O}\left(n^{2}\right)$
  3. $\mathrm{O}(n \log n)$
  4. $\mathrm{O}\left(n^{2} \log n \right)$

  2. $\overline{(\overline{X \oplus Y)} \oplus Z}$
     
  3. $(X \oplus Y) \oplus \overline{Z}$

Suppose we have a relation $R(A, B)$ with one tuple, both of whose components are NULL:

  1. (NULL,NULL)
  2. (NULL,0)
  3. $(\mathrm{NULL}, 1)$
